extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers (readers of AP/press coverage of postwar government and veterans' issues)
extracted.subtask_description: An Associated Press news article covering post‑World War II U.S. government reorganization, veterans' transportation/housing problems, legislation and policy developments. Intended as straight news reporting of official actions, statements, hearings and bills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies exempted from reorganization
rubrics_metrics.description: Six agencies are exempted from reorganization: the Interstate Commerce Commission, Federal Trade Commission, Securities and Exchange Commission, National Mediation Board, National Railroad Adjustment Board and Railroad Retirement Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These agencies are exempt except that additional duties, agencies and employees may be shifted to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies to be handled separately in reorganization plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain agencies must be dealt with separately and under plans which would affect no other agency if any effort is made to reorganize them: the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Communications Commission, the Tariff Commission and Veterans Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorganization proposals relating to these agencies require separate plans that do not alter or affect other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau of the Budget's role in preparing reorganization plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The director of the Bureau of the Budget has been instructed to obtain the recommendations of all departments and establishments covered by the act and to take the lead in preparing the necessary reorganization plans for the President's consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He will work with the Director of War Mobilization and Reconversion insofar as the plans involve reconversion of the war agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected limits and aims of reorganization savings
rubrics_metrics.description: While the act may result in some reduction of administrative expenditures, it is not considered probable that overall savings will reach as much as 25% as suggested; administrative expenditures are only a small proportion of government cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial savings in government expenditures can come only from reductions in government programs through the normal budgetary and appropriations processes, not through reorganization action. The primary results will be increased effectiveness, consistency, coordination and a simpler relation between agencies and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate War Investigating Committee oversight of veterans' transportation delays
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee ordered an investigation of delays in homeward transportation for veterans landing at West Coast ports, called public hearings and summoned Col. J. Monroe Johnson, director of defense transportation, to appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearings were scheduled promptly to examine the bottleneck and causes preventing veterans from reaching their homes promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarantine procedure for contagious cases aboard troopships
rubrics_metrics.description: When a service member aboard a troopship was found ill with smallpox, the vessel was ordered to put in at Portland where it would be under quarantine until Dec. 26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected personnel were to be quarantined and additional staging areas opened to manage stranded troops.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEPC authority and limits under executive orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive order gives the Fair Employment Practice Committee (FEPC) continuing authority to investigate private industry discriminations until June 30, 1946, but the committee no longer has authority to issue directives in private industry except in Government work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FEPC officials said the committee will hold hearings; legislation is pending to make FEPC permanent but the House Rules Committee has blocked such a bill so far. FEPC received $250,000 under war agencies appropriation to continue work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential directive on rehiring and anti-discrimination in reconversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The President directed heads of departments and agencies to analyze personnel policies to see that no racial discrimination is practiced in rehiring of temporary job workers; observed that loyal and qualified employees had been refused transfer and reemployment solely because of race and creed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such discrimination is a violation of civil service rules and existing law; the directive is intended to prevent discriminatory rehiring during reconversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles and provisions in the new Atomic Energy Control bill (McMahon)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill declares that development and utilization of atomic energy shall be directed toward improving the public welfare, increasing standard of living, and strengthening free competition; it endorses free dissemination of basic scientific information, federally conducted research where necessary, and study of social, political and economic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details include placing direction in the hands of a commission of presidential appointees and provisions to balance public benefit with private enterprise and dissemination of technical information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans' preference in new government housing program
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal officials working out the housing program said veterans are expected to obtain the lion's share of homes built under the new program, particularly homes costing $10,000 or less; veterans may obtain an estimated 75% of homes built in 1946.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will be no priority for veterans on homes built to sell at more than $10,000. Builders may be required to offer homes to veterans first for a stated period (reported as probably 30 days) before disposing of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eviction and rent‑control procedural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Landlords desiring to remodel or demolish hotels or rooming houses to obtain eviction certificates must get them from area-rent directors before dispossessing permanent tenants. Area‑rent directors issuing eviction certificates are authorized to impose a waiting period up to either three or six months (maximum in the area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rent ceilings may apply to rooms in newly constructed hotels and rooming houses; converted buildings and rooms are subject to revised controls and waiting periods to protect tenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of wartime rationing and priority powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation was sent to the White House extending until July 1 the wartime rationing and priority powers given the President and continuing most other powers under the Second War Powers Act, including waiving navigation laws to allow overloading of troopships returning veterans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate leaders sought a longer extension to January 1, 1947, but the conference draft approved extension only until July 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganization of Veterans Administration medical division
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress sent to the White House a measure reorganizing the medical division of the Veterans Administration, establishing the office of chief medical examiner, a deputy, assistants, and a director of nursing service with specified salaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measure restructures VA medical administration and sets pay scales for the new positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Court procedure in Yamashita petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court asked experts in military law for help in deciding petitions from General Tomoyuki Yamashita and called for arguments; it granted a stay of execution pending its final decision and ordered that all action on the requests be held until argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court scheduled arguments and sought briefs on whether the military commission's actions should be reviewed by civil courts, whether the case should be removed to civil courts, and related jurisdictional and authority questions.
